title: CORRECTION to v3 verdict: actual work (output tokens) ON≈OFF (0.95×) — the "65% less work / net 0.35×" was a metric artifact
summary: Supersedes the work-reduction claim in note-mq70mq8w. Prompted by the user asking 'how much actual work token ON vs OFF'. Computed the clean per-component breakdown from v3 transcripts (n=5 each): OUTPUT tokens (the real 'work generated', unaffected by attribution bucketing) — OFF 10,567 vs ON 10,062 = 0.95× (EQUAL). fresh input 0.96×. cache_creation 1.02×. cache_read OFF 290,147 vs ON 342,475 = 1.18× — ON's ONLY material extra cost. CONCLUSION: the agent did the SAME amount of work with or without graph context; ON's entire overhead is cache_read from re-attending the loaded get_learnings payload + tool schemas every turn. The earlier 'cost net ON/OFF = 0.35× → agent does ~65% less work' was a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT: net = gross − orchestrator-attributed, and the attributionMcpServer tagging is 'sticky' (spans post-call messages), so it absorbed most of ON's cache_read into the 'plumbing' bucket, making ON's net spuriously tiny. Output tokens are the honest work proxy and show parity. REVISED OVERALL FINDING (v1→v2→v3): on self-solvable tasks the graph context produced NO measured work-reduction and NO quality delta (both arms equal output, both solved 5/5); the orchestrator's cost is purely cache_read of loaded context, which lean payload reduces to ~cost parity (1.03×) — but with no benefit to offset it on these tasks. The hypothesized benefit (context lets the agent skip dead-ends) was never demonstrated because no spec was hard enough to require the graph. LESSON: use output_tokens (or fresh input+output) as the work measure, NOT gross−plumbing 'net', which is confounded by sticky MCP attribution of cache_read.
